title: Re-dispose all eighteen rule files under a behaviour test; B1 dissolved rather than resolved
context: Blocker B1 recorded that check 8.5's 13,000-byte ceiling was unreachable: the six rules section 5.2 kept totalled 11,698 bytes and CLAUDE.md another 2,070, so the subtotal was 13,768 before the new delegation rule existed. Three resolutions were costed - trim no-direct-db-access in place, split it to a skill, or raise the ceiling.U+000AU+000AThe user rejected the framing rather than picking one. Their challenge: pillars restates a default Claude already follows, no-comments is 1,459 bytes for a one-line rule, coding-style is generic, security duplicates the vibesec skill and a security-reviewer agent, and no-direct-db-access should say only "never connect to a live database, author SQL for a human" - a local test container is not a live database and migrations are not the prohibition.U+000AU+000AThe challenge was correct and exposed a structural inconsistency. Revisions 1 through 3 disposed the eighteen files on scope alone: does this apply to every piece of work. That test cut twelve as situational and kept six without anyone asking whether they changed behaviour - which is the test the spec's own section 0.2 implies, and the stated reason patterns.md was deleted.
options: Amend section 5.2 now: add a second test (does this change behaviour, versus restating a default or duplicating a mechanism that already binds) and re-run the disposition across all eighteen files. Supersedes B1 and its three options.
Keep the spec as approved, take R2 to unblock step 8, and file the preamble audit as separate follow-up work with its own thread.
outcome: First option, selected by the user. SPEC revision 4 adds test T2 alongside the existing scope test T1, and applies both to all eighteen files. All six formerly-kept files change disposition.U+000AU+000Apillars.md is deleted outright - its rule is already a CLAUDE.md bullet and the file is only rationale. no-comments.md, coding-style.md and security.md compress to the part that binds (~300, ~300, ~400 bytes), keeping respectively the functional carve-out without which Claude will not write a shebang, the immutability rule which is genuinely non-default in Python and JavaScript, and the response protocol. memory-discipline.md is the only one of the six passing T2 intact. no-direct-db-access.md is rescoped from 4,293 to ~600.U+000AU+000ATwo mechanism findings made the compressions defensible rather than merely smaller. secret-scanner.sh already enforces "no hardcoded secrets" as a PreToolUse hook on Edit|Write, so the checklist line restating it is redundant at class M. block-destructive-bash.sh already denies hosted Supabase connections AND states the local-container exception verbatim in its own deny message, which is why the 1,377-byte carve-out can be deleted rather than relocated.U+000AU+000ATwo gaps are accepted, not closed, and recorded as SPEC 10.5. vibesec triggers on web application code, so a non-web project gets no depth from it - mitigated by wiring vibesec into security-reviewer, a gap the earlier revisions never noticed. And the bash gate matches the Supabase CLI path only, not psql or a raw DATABASE_URL, which is why the general prohibition stays as prose instead of deferring to the hook.U+000AU+000ABudget: 51,740 bytes to ~5,850, roughly 12,935 tokens to ~1,460. That beats section 1.2's stated target of ~2,520 rather than approximating it, which no B1 resolution did. B1 is therefore dissolved rather than resolved: check 8.5 keeps its 13,000 value, now a circuit breaker at 2.2x headroom in the section 0.3 sense rather than a target to squeeze under. Tightening it to just above the new figure would make it a change-detector failing on the next legitimate addition.U+000AU+000ALanded as commit 0d8722c0 on branch docs/agent-architecture-spec. 24 readiness checks pass with zero failures, including that all eighteen byte figures in section 5.2 match disk.
